translate_en|mods/PixelStrikeIndicator/4:
<RGB:1,1,1>The same, for animals. It is a
separate setting, so you can allow
one kind and refuse the other.

<RGB:1,1,1>Off: no bars. Only When Hurt: a bar
appears once an animal is hurt.
Always: every animal near a player
has one.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>Animals all share one maximum
health, so the bar is right the
first time a player looks. The
server sends nothing for it.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Animals have no toughness bar. The
game gives them no toughness value.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>Players start on Only When Hurt.
Always would put a bar over every
chicken on a farm.
Maximum Zombie And Animal Bar Range, In Tiles

<RGB:1,1,1>How far from a player a health bar
may still be drawn. Zombies and
animals both.

<RGB:1,1,1>Each player has a slider too, and
this is the limit on it. 60 is as
far as the mod ever draws a bar, so
60 means no limit.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>A player's slider is a share of
their own screen, and a wide screen
shows more ground. This setting is
in tiles, so it is the same distance
for everybody.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>A small number makes players walk
close before they can judge a
zombie. 4 is the floor, so a zombie
standing beside a player always has
a bar.

<RGB:1,1,1>Turn this off to hide every zombie,
animal, vehicle and player bar. It
overrides all bar settings below.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>The settings below do not change.
Turn this back on and each bar
returns at its previous allowed
level.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>This also hides percentages,
toughness bars, friend or foe frames
and right click inspection.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>Zombie health sharing pauses too, so
the server does no work for bars
nobody can see.
Allow BOOM!! When An Explosion Hits Nothing

<RGB:1,1,1>The same word and star with no
number under it, on the tile an
explosion went off on.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>It is drawn only when the blast
damaged nothing at all. When it did,
the numbers over what it caught
already say where it was.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>It is there so a bomb that misses
still says where it went off, which
the smoke and the fire hide.

<RGB:1,1,1>A critical hit is a strong hit the
game gives at random. It gets a
bigger number in pale gold, a coral
star behind it, and CRITICAL!!
above.

<RGB:1,1,1>With this off, a critical hit uses
the ordinary damage number instead,
if those numbers are allowed.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>Melee weapons only. A gun that rolls
a critical hit turns it into a shot
to the head, which has its own line
below.
Allow Numbers For Damage Players Deal

<RGB:1,1,1>The white number over anything a
player hits. This is the main thing
the mod draws.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>Critical hits, headshots, instant
kills and explosion damage are
versions of that number. Turning
this off removes them too, whatever
their own lines say.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off for the health bars and
no numbers.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>It leaves alone the damage a player
takes, healing, fire on zombies,
MISS and LEVEL UP!!. Each of those
has a line of its own.

<RGB:1,1,1>Only the displayed number changes.
This never changes how much damage a
weapon, fire, fall or vehicle
actually does.

<RGB:1,1,1>The number over a target is its
damage times this. It makes 1.5
damage appear as 150 at the default
100.

<RGB:1,1,1>Each player has a slider and this is
the limit on it. They can pick less,
never more. 1000 is as far as the
slider goes, so 1000 means no limit.
They all start at 100.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>A strong axe hit is about 1.5
damage. At 100 it reads 150, at 10
it reads 15, at 1 it reads 2. The
mod never draws under 1, so a low
number rounds a light hit and a
heavy one to the same digit.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Fire, falls, cars and healing use a
tenth of this. A door, a window, a
barricade, furniture and a tree are
not multiplied at all.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>Players may choose a lower
multiplier, but never one above this
server limit.
Allow Numbers For Fire, Falls And Collisions

<RGB:1,1,1>Damage from fire, from falling, and
from hitting or being hit by a car.
This is on top of the damage from
being struck.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>Only those. Bleeding, infection,
hunger and thirst hurt a player too,
and none of them are shown: each
would print a number every second
until the player is well.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>These appear only when numbers for
damage players take are also
allowed.

<RGB:1,1,1>Damage from a pipe bomb, a grenade
or anything else that goes off is
drawn like a critical hit: a bigger
number, a star behind it, and BOOM!!
over the top.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>One lands on each thing the blast
caught, so a bomb in a crowd is a
lot of them at once. Players have a
switch for the word on its own if
that is too much.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off and explosion damage
uses the ordinary damage number
instead, if those numbers are
allowed.

<RGB:1,1,1>A bullet in a zombie's head gets a
bigger light blue number, a star
behind it, and HEADSHOT!! above.

<RGB:1,1,1>With this off, a headshot uses the
ordinary damage number instead, if
those numbers are allowed.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>The game makes headshot damage 3
times larger. That is why the number
is so much bigger than the others,
and why the zombie usually dies.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Guns only. A melee weapon shows the
critical hit effect instead.

<RGB:1,1,1>Health coming back shows as a green
number beside a player, the way
damage shows in red.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>The game sends no message when a
player heals, so the mod watches
their health instead. Healing is
slow and steady, so the mod adds it
up and shows one number instead of
many small ones.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>This is health coming back, not a
wound being treated. A bandage stops
the bleeding first, and the numbers
come over the hours after that.

<RGB:1,1,1>The most a player may see. Each
player then picks their own under
Options, Mods, Pixel Health Bars.
They can pick less than this, never
more.

<RGB:1,1,1>Off: no bars. Only When Hurt: a bar
appears after the first hit. Always:
every zombie near a player has one.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>A bar is one zombie's health.
Zombies are not all equally strong,
so a full bar is not always a strong
zombie.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Off takes the toughness bar and the
right click check with it. Both are
drawn on the health bar.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>Animals have a setting of their own,
on the next line.

<RGB:1,1,1>A number from 100 to 0 beside a
health bar. It can appear on zombie,
animal, vehicle and player bars.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>For a zombie, animal or player it
shows health left. For a vehicle it
shows Overall Condition.

<RGB:1,1,1>Each player chooses the four kinds
separately. This switch is the
server limit for all four.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off to leave every bar
visual only, with no exact number
beside it.

<RGB:1,1,1>A player holds the right mouse
button and points at a zombie. That
zombie shows its bar, even one
nobody has hit yet.

<RGB:1,1,1>It is a way to check one zombie
without leaving every bar on the
screen.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off and a player sees only
the bars their own setting gives
them.

<RGB:1,1,1>A knife pushed into a zombie's jaw
kills it at once, whatever health
was left. That kill gets its own
number, a star behind it, and
INSTAKILL!! above.

<RGB:1,1,1>With this off, the kill uses the
ordinary damage number instead, if
those numbers are allowed.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>Melee weapons and knives only. The
game does it when a zombie stands
close in front of a player, and it
is the same moment that can leave
the knife stuck in it.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>It beats a critical hit. When one
hit is both, the mod shows this
word, because this one is rarer.

<RGB:1,1,1>LEVEL UP!! appears over a player,
with wings behind it, when one of
their skills reaches a new level.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>It does not say which skill. The
skill panel already does, and a
skill name would have to be drawn in
a game font instead of the one the
player picked.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off and only the skill panel
and the sound the game already plays
tell the player.
Allow MISS After A Missed Melee Swing

<RGB:1,1,1>When a player swings a melee weapon
and hits nothing, the white word
MISS lands where they stand.

<RGB:1,1,1>It only appears when a zombie was
close enough to be the target, so
swinging at empty space stays quiet.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>Melee weapons only. A gun cannot
miss in this game: a shot either
hits something or is never fired.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off and a missed swing shows
nothing.
Allow Friend Or Foe Bar Frames

<RGB:1,1,1>The frame around a health bar. Dark
red on a character that will attack
the player, dark blue on one that
will not.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>It reads an NPC mod's own data. With
no NPC mod on the server nothing is
ever drawn differently and this
setting does nothing at all.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>It tells a player which side an NPC
is on before that NPC acts. Turn it
off where working that out is meant
to be part of the danger.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>It costs nothing. The data is
already in hand for the bar being
drawn.

<RGB:1,1,1>Turn this off to hide every damage
number, banner, burst and gun hit
marker. It overrides all number
settings below.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>The settings below do not change.
Turn this back on and each effect
returns at its previous allowed
setting.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Health bars are separate and stay
available.
Allow Numbers For Damage To Objects

<RGB:1,1,1>A number over a door, a window, a
barricade, a piece of furniture or a
tree when a player hits it, where a
number over a zombie would be.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>It is the health the swing took off
that door, not what a zombie would
have taken. A door is counted on a
scale of its own and the displayed
damage multiplier leaves it alone.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>A multiplayer client is never told
what a swing took off a door,
because the server settles that
alone. These numbers are for single
player and for the host.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>Players start with this off.
Breaking into a house is a long run
of swings and a lot of numbers.

<RGB:1,1,1>A bar over a player's own character,
in the same place and the same
colours as a zombie's.

<RGB:1,1,1>Off: no bar. Only When Hurt: it
appears once that player is injured.
Always: it is always there.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>A player sees their own and nobody
else's. The server sends nothing for
it, so it costs nothing however many
people are on.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>This is body health, 0 to 100, the
number the health panel shows. A
zombie's bar uses another scale, and
the two do not compare.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>Players start on Only When Hurt, so
an unhurt character carries nothing.

<RGB:1,1,1>A bar over a zombie, animal, vehicle
or NPC the player cannot see, such
as behind a wall or in a dark room.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>Normally the mod hides a bar
whenever the player's character
cannot see its target.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off to make this impossible
for everyone. A hurt target then
loses its bar out of sight and gets
it back when seen again.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>Players start with this off, so
nobody sees through a wall unless
they ask for it.
Allow Numbers For Damage Players Take

<RGB:1,1,1>The red number beside a player when
something hurts them.

<RGB:1,1,1>It flies to the left, and the damage
they deal flies to the right, so the
two are easy to tell apart.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off and a player sees only
the damage they deal. Fire, falls
and car damage go with it.
Sync Starting Zombie Health To Players

<RGB:1,1,1>Every player sees the same health
bar and the same toughness bar on a
zombie, because the server tells
them how much health it started
with.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>A player's game can see how much
health a zombie has now, but never
how much it had at the start.
Without this, a zombie somebody else
already fought looks unhurt to
everyone who meets it later, and its
toughness bar looks short.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off to save traffic. Each
player then uses the most health
they have seen themselves, and two
players can see different bars on
one zombie.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>It costs one small request per
player every few seconds, and only
while that player has zombies close
enough to have a bar.

<RGB:1,1,1>A second, thinner bar under the
health bar. It does not move when a
zombie is hurt.

<RGB:1,1,1>It shows how much damage that zombie
can take in all. A long bar needs
many more hits than a short one, so
a player can decide before they
attack.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>It only says something when
Toughness, under Zombie Lore, is
Random. That is what Apocalypse
uses. On the other settings every
zombie is nearly alike.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off to keep a zombie's
strength a surprise.

<RGB:1,1,1>A bar over a car, drawn like a
zombie's and in the same colours.

<RGB:1,1,1>Off: no bars. Only When Damaged: a
bar appears once a car has taken
something. Always: every car near a
player has one.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>It is the Overall Condition the
mechanics window prints, 0 to 100,
worked out the same way. The bar and
that window never disagree.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Each player reads it from their own
game and the server sends nothing.
How far it reaches and how many cars
are watched are their settings.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>Players start on Off, so this
matters only once somebody turns it
on.

<RGB:1,1,1>A number over a car when one of its
parts loses condition: a zombie
beating on the bonnet, a crash, a
bullet, or a window going in.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>Glass is drawn in its own colour,
and each number lands at the part
that took it, so the bonnet and a
door read apart.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>It is read off the cars around a
player a few times a second and asks
the server for nothing. A
multiplayer client already knows
every part's condition, so it works
there.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>Players start with this off.

<RGB:1,1,1>When a zombie opens a wound, the
word for it lands where the player
stands: BITTEN!!, SCRATCHED or
LACERATED.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>It is what the health panel would
say, a moment sooner and without
opening it. It never says whether a
bite has infected them. The game
keeps that hidden and so does the
mod.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off to make a player open
the health panel to learn what a
zombie did to them.

<RGB:0.800,1.000,0.000>It costs almost nothing: three
counts the game already keeps, read
twice a second.

<RGB:1,1,1>A burning zombie shows an orange
number for the damage the fire is
doing. A player can then see whether
the fire is working or only making
light.

<RGB:0.100,0.800,1.000>The game sends no message when fire
hurts a zombie, so the mod watches
the health of the zombies nearby. It
covers only zombies close enough to
have a bar, and only while they
burn.

<RGB:1.000,0.700,0.200>Turn it off and a player has to
judge the fire by eye.
Combine Rapid Hits Into One Number

Adds rapid hits of the same type on the same target into one number. Different targets and local players stay separate. Critical hits, healing and fire never combine with ordinary hits. Starts off, and presets leave it unchanged.
Rapid Hit Window, 250 Milliseconds Is Normal
Where An Animal's Bar Is Drawn
The number beside an animal's bar, on a switch of its own, so a farm can stay plain while the zombies carry one.
Base Height For Every Health Bar, 100 Is Normal
Max Zombie And Animal Bars Per Type, Nearest First
Where A Zombie's Bar Is Drawn
Zombie And Animal Bar Range, 100 Is Screen Edge
Base Width For Every Bar, 100 Is Normal
Turn this off to hide every zombie, animal, vehicle and player bar. The settings below do not change, so turning this back on restores the same setup. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Show A Star Behind That Empty-Hit BOOM!!
The star behind that word. Requires Show BOOM!! When An Explosion Hits Nothing. Turn it off to keep the word on its own.
Show BOOM!! When An Explosion Hits Nothing

The same word and star with no number under it, on the tile the blast went off on. It is drawn only when the blast damaged nothing at all, because when it did the numbers already say where it was. It is there so a bomb that misses still tells you where it landed. A server can turn this off for everyone.
The colour of the star behind a critical hit. It is a setting of its own, so the star can sit under the number instead of matching it.
The star that opens behind the number. Requires Show Critical Hit Number, Star And Banner. It is the loudest part of the effect. Turn it off to keep the pale gold number and the word without it.
Changes both the critical hit number and the word CRITICAL!!. The star behind them has its own colour setting below.
Show Critical Hit Number, Star And Banner

A critical hit is a strong hit the game gives you at random. It gets a bigger number in pale gold, a star, and CRITICAL!! above. Melee only: a gun turns its critical hits into headshots. This is the main switch for the critical hit settings below. A server can turn this off for everyone.
The word above the number. Requires Show Critical Hit Number, Star And Banner. Turn it off to keep the bigger pale gold number and the star. The number then flies the path any other number takes.
Show Numbers For Damage You Deal

Shows the ordinary white number over a character or animal you hit. Critical hits, headshots, instant kills and explosion damage are special versions of this number, so this switch controls them too. Other number sections and health bars remain available. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Include Fire, Falls And Collision Damage

Also shows damage you take from fire, falling or a vehicle collision. Bleeding, infection, hunger and thirst are not shown. Requires Show Numbers For Damage You Take. A server can turn this off for everyone.

Turns on the master switch, puts every bar on Always and shows every optional bar detail. Range, limits, size, position, colours and unseen-target visibility stay unchanged. Server limits still apply.
Turns on the master switch and every number, banner, burst and hit marker in this section. Font, size, timing, motion, aggregation and colours stay unchanged. Server limits still apply.
The colour of the star behind it. It starts a hot orange.
The star behind the number. Requires Show Explosion Number, Star And BOOM!!. Turn it off to keep the bigger number and the word without it.
The colour of the number and of the word over it. It starts a pale amber, hot but light enough to read over fire and smoke.
Show Explosion Number, Star And BOOM!!

Damage from anything that explodes is drawn the way a critical hit is: a bigger number, a star, and BOOM!! over the top. One lands on each thing the blast caught. Turn it off and that damage goes back to an ordinary white number. This is the main switch for the explosion settings below. A server can turn this off for everyone.

The word above the number. Requires Show Explosion Number, Star And BOOM!!. Turn it off to keep the bigger number and the star. A bomb in a crowd is one of these on every zombie it caught, so this is the one to reach for if that is a lot.
The colour of the number on a burning zombie. You need Show Fire Damage On Zombies to see it at all.
Seconds Combined Into Each Fire Number

A broken window is drawn in this colour instead. It starts a strong cyan, because a window going in is the easiest car damage to miss. It is deeper than the pale blue a door or a headshot uses, so the three do not blur.
The colour of the star behind a headshot. It is a setting of its own, so the star can sit under the number instead of matching it.
The star that opens behind the number. Requires Show Headshot Number, Star And Banner. It is the loudest part of the effect. Turn it off to keep the light blue number and the word without it.
Changes both the headshot number and the word HEADSHOT!!. The star behind them has its own colour setting below.
Show Headshot Number, Star And Banner

A bullet in a zombie's head gets a bigger light blue number, a star, and HEADSHOT!! above. The game makes that damage 3 times larger, so it usually kills. This is the main switch for the headshot settings below. A server can turn this off for everyone.
The word above the number. Requires Show Headshot Number, Star And Banner. Turn it off to keep the bigger light blue number and the star.
The colour of the heart behind a healing number. You need Show The Healing Heart to see it at all.
A heart that opens behind the number. This starts off. Healing comes slowly over time rather than in one moment, so there is no moment to mark.
Changes the number that shows health returning. The optional heart behind it has its own colour setting below.
Health coming back, as a green number beside you. Healing is slow, so the mod adds it up and shows one number instead of many small ones. A server can turn this off for everyone.
The number beside a zombie's bar, counting down from 100 to 0, in the same font as the damage numbers. A server can turn this off for everyone.
The colour of that number. You see this one most, so it starts white, which reads over any ground.
Show A Hit Marker When A Bullet Lands

A small cross at your cursor for a moment when a bullet lands on something. It takes the headshot star colour when the bullet took the head. Guns only: a melee swing has its number and needs no mark. Requires Show Numbers For Damage You Deal.
The colour of that number. Fire, falls and cars use it too.
Right Click To Inspect A Zombie Bar
Hold the right mouse button and point at a zombie to see its bar, even one nobody has hit yet. A server can turn this off for everyone.
The colour of the star behind an instant kill. It is a setting of its own, so the star can sit under the number instead of matching it.
The star that opens behind the number. Requires Show Instant Kill Number, Star And Banner. It is the loudest part of the effect. Turn it off to keep the number and the word without it.
Changes both the instant kill number and the word INSTAKILL!!. The star behind them has its own colour setting below.
Show Instant Kill Number, Star And Banner

A knife pushed into a zombie's jaw kills it at once. That kill gets a bigger number in bone white, a star, and INSTAKILL!! above. When one hit is both, you see this instead of a critical hit. This is the main switch for the instant kill settings below. A server can turn this off for everyone.
The word above the number. Requires Show Instant Kill Number, Star And Banner. Turn it off to keep the bigger bone white number and the star.
The colour of the wings behind the words. It is a setting of its own, so they can sit under the words instead of matching them.

The pair of wings that opens behind the words. Turn them off to keep the words on their own. The four hits that land use a star. This one uses wings, healing uses a heart, and a missed swing uses a puff of air.
The colour of the words LEVEL UP!!. They have no number under them, so this is their whole colour.
Show LEVEL UP!! When A Skill Gains A Level
The words LEVEL UP!! appear over you when one of your skills reaches a new level. It does not say which skill. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Show Recent Health Or Condition Loss

Shows recent health loss on zombie and animal bars, and recent condition loss on vehicle bars, as a white strip. The strip pauses briefly, then drains down to the current value. Your own bar has a separate switch below.
Pixel Health Bars: Show Basics Only

Turns on the master switch and keeps a plain bar on hurt zombies plus right click inspection. Other bars and optional details turn off. Range, limits, size, position, colours and unseen-target visibility stay unchanged.
Pixel Strike Indicator: Show Basics Only

Turns on the master switch and keeps only damage you deal and damage you take, including fire, falls and collisions. Other effects turn off. Font, size, timing, motion, aggregation and colours stay unchanged.
The colour of the puff around the word MISS. You need Show The Miss Puff to see it at all.
A ring of sharp air streaks opens around the word, like the swing cut straight past its target. This starts off: a missed swing is the one thing worth the least noise.
The colour of the word MISS. It has no number under it, so this is its whole colour.
Show MISS After A Missed Melee Swing
When you swing a melee weapon and hit nothing, the white word MISS lands where you stand. It only appears when a zombie was close enough to be your target. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Where An NPC's Bar Is Drawn
The frame around an NPC's bar when that NPC is hostile to you. It starts a dark red, deep enough that the health inside it still reads.
The same frame on an NPC who is not hostile. It starts a dark blue, the furthest thing from the red without lighting the frame up.
Colour NPC Frames By Friend Or Foe

With an NPC mod installed, the frame around the bar turns dark red on a character that will attack you and dark blue on one that will not. The bar itself still shows health the same way. With no NPC mod this does nothing.

Turn this off to hide every damage number, banner, burst and hit marker. The settings below do not change, so turning this back on restores the same setup. Health bars are controlled separately. A server can turn this off for everyone.
The colour of that number. It starts a pale steel blue, so a door reads apart from the white over a zombie at a glance.
Show Numbers For Damage To Objects

A number when you hit a door, a window, a barricade, furniture or a tree. It is the health your swing took off. A door is counted on a scale of its own, so it does not read like the number over a zombie and the displayed multiplier leaves it alone. It starts off, because breaking into a house is a lot of swings. On a multiplayer client it stays quiet, because the server settles a door and never says by how much. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Your Bar Height, 100 Matches The Base Height
Head Or Feet For Your Character Bar
Your Bar Width, 100 Matches The Base Width
Your Health Bar: When It Appears
Show Exact Health On Your Bar
The number beside your own bar, counting down from 100. It is body health, the number the health panel shows, and it has a switch of its own so a zombie's bar can stay plain.
The white strip on your own bar, the same as the one on a zombie's, on a switch of its own.
Blocks In Your Bar, 0 Means No Dividers
How Long Popups Stay, 100 Is Normal
Open or close a draggable preview of zombie, animal, vehicle and player bars. It updates from unsaved settings while you adjust them. Select Apply to save the changes.
Previewing unsaved settings. Apply to save them.
Open or close a draggable preview of your numbers and banners. It updates from unsaved settings while you adjust them. Select Apply to save the changes.
Keeps numbers and banners in place while they fade. Removes bouncing, drifting, growth and burst animation without hiding any effect. Presets leave this preference unchanged.
Restores every Pixel Health Bars setting to its original value. Pixel Strike Indicator settings do not change.
Restores every Pixel Strike Indicator setting to its original value. Pixel Health Bars settings do not change.

Allows bars on unseen zombies, animals, vehicles and NPCs, including targets behind walls or in dark rooms. Starts off, so world bars normally appear only while your character can see their target. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Blocks In Non-Player Bars, 0 Means Plain
Show Numbers For Damage You Take
The red number beside you when something hurts you. It flies to the left, and the damage you deal flies to the right, so the two never look the same. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Number And Banner Size, 100 Is Normal
Font Used For Numbers And Banners

A thinner bar under the health bar. It shows how much damage that zombie can take in all, not how hurt it is now. It only says something when Toughness, under Zombie Lore, is set to Random. A server can turn this off for everyone.
One pale line across the toughness bar, at the total toughness of an ordinary zombie. A bar longer than the line is a tougher zombie, shorter is a weaker one.
Vehicle Bar Height, 100 Matches The Base Height
Where A Car's Bar Is Drawn
Vehicle Bar Width, 100 Matches The Base Width
Vehicle Condition Bars: When They Appear
The colour of that number. It starts a soft violet, the one part of the palette nothing else uses, so a car is never mistaken for a door or for a hit.

A number over a car when a part loses condition: a zombie hitting it, a crash, a bullet, or a window breaking. It lands at the part that took it, so the bonnet, a door and a wheel read apart. This is condition, 0 to 100, on a scale of its own, and the displayed multiplier leaves it alone. It starts off. It watches the nearest few cars around you and asks the server for nothing, so it works in multiplayer. A server can turn this off for everyone.
The number beside a car's bar. It is the same Overall Condition the mechanics window prints, without opening the bonnet.
Cars Watched For Numbers And Bars, Nearest First
Car Number And Bar Range, In Tiles
The colour of those three words. It starts the same red as the damage you take, because a wound is damage you took.
Show Wound Type: BITTEN!!, SCRATCHED, LACERATED

When a zombie opens a wound on you, the word for it lands where you stand. It is what the health panel would tell you, a moment sooner and without opening it. It never says whether a bite has infected you, because the game keeps that hidden. A server can turn this off for everyone.

A burning zombie shows an orange number for the damage the fire is doing. Fire takes the same amount from every zombie, so the number looks the same on all of them. A server can turn this off for everyone.
